claims.sourceText: Joint federal statement, 17 December 2024, reported by The Debrief
claims.text: Joint statement of 17 December 2024 by DoD, DHS, FBI and FAA: 'We have not identified anything anomalous, and do not assess the activity to date to present a national security or public safety risk over the civilian airspace in New Jersey or other states.'

edges.label: Task force stood up in August 2025 after two years of unattributed incursions
edges.note: A standing joint interagency task force under a general officer is the institutional refutation of the hobbyist explanation issued eight months earlier.

b.label: New Jersey and East Coast Drone Wave (Nov-Dec 2024)

edges.label: Twelve months apart; the second wave was publicly resolved, the first never was
edges.note: Langley produced no attribution and no public explanation; New Jersey produced a four-agency statement attributing 5,000 reports to hobbyists and misidentifications on the basis of about 100 leads.

edges.label: Four-agency joint statement of 17 December 2024
edges.note: DoD, DHS, FBI and FAA: 'We have not identified anything anomalous, and do not assess the activity to date to present a national security or public safety risk.' The same statement conceded limited sightings over restricted military airspace, contradicting earlier White House denials.

a.label: New Jersey and East Coast Drone Wave (Nov-Dec 2024)

edges.label: Wright-Patterson closed its airspace for nearly four hours during the wave
edges.note: The 14-15 December 2024 airspace closure over unauthorized drone activity occurred days before the federal statement that nothing anomalous had been identified.
